name: Identity number
issuer: the Minister responsible for home affairs (the Ministry of Home Affairs, Immigration, Safety and Security), in the population register
note: Namibia's Identification Act 21 of 1996 (in force from 18 May 2001 by GN 95/2001), read 2026-10-30 in the Legal Assistance Centre's annotated copy of the statute (the Act's own text; NamibLII answered with a Cloudflare check and wasn't opened). S. 2: the Minister keeps a population register of Namibian citizens and of non-citizens holding permanent residence permits. S. 4: on issuing an identity document under s. 5(1), the Minister assigns its holder an identity number consisting of eleven figures. S. 5(1): the identity document is issued on application to a person who has attained 16 and whose name is in the register. So the length is eleven, the pattern eleven digits ('figures'), `when` application, `from` 16, `who` citizens and residents (the game's residents standing for the permanent residents the Act names). No check rule, fee or time is stated for the number (the card's fee is the identity documents engine's). The Civil Registration and Identification Act 13 of 2024 (signed 13 December 2024) will repeal it; LAC's copy of that Act says it has not yet been brought into force. Its s. 7 has the Registrar-General assign a unique identifying number to every person whose birth is registered, and s. 49(5) lets an identity document carry either that identifier or an identity number of a prescribed number of digits; when it takes effect, the number's terms here must be read again. The Namibia Revenue Agency's pages (individual tax, FAQs, read 2026-10-30) say a salaried person earning over N$100,000 a year should register as a taxpayer, but give no form for the tax number, so the identity number is the one modelled. Both texts are the Legal Assistance Centre's annotated reproductions, so they are held as secondary, quoting the Acts as NamibLII publishes them (behind a bot check from here; the lead, 2026-10-30).
